title: Conserved budget core
description: Objective: implement hierarchical accounts, reservations, protected proof/review reserves, usage settlement, and explicit measurement coverage. Deliverable: packages/scheduler budget modules with conservation and concurrent-admission property tests. NOT in scope: billing APIs, guessed token costs, scheduler fairness, or UI charts. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry and Policy approval core. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/budget/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: Randomized reserve, activate, settle, cancel, and restart schedules never mint or overspend budget.
UNKNOWN measurement remains UNKNOWN, never zero, and blocks policy when required.
Verification and independent-review reserves are protected before execution admission.
The focused scheduler typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.
reopenReason: Governor: dependencies verified landed. Runtime contract registry DONE; Policy approval core is in REVIEW with its code committed — packages/core/src/policy is tracked (approval-contract.ts, policy-contract.ts, policy-evaluation.ts). I sent this back to BACKLOG earlier today precisely because packages/core/src/policy did not exist; that condition has cleared. Owns packages/scheduler/src/budget/**, file-disjoint from the three sibling scheduler subtrees (authority, dependencies, admission). Plan the budget contract against Policy's committed interface, not against an assumed one.

comments.content: SPIDR sizing decision: the original account+reservation+measurement+settlement+randomized-hardening scope is ~1.8–2.0k LOC and cannot meet the <=400-LOC/1–3-file task rail while keeping production and tests <=250 lines. Created five file-disjoint child tasks: task-7dc2e4870d7d4096a1be7b5991e50e94 (contract), task-a5def097bcb7495e935204bd845160b4 (hierarchical ledger), task-318c0732094c417f96932b5c83e7388b (protected reservations), task-5ee5b801127a4536a6e770abc6e83e9e (measurement truth), task-3602672fd0c74de6b6fc72f90e1745c8 (settlement). After those land, this parent becomes the explicit final integration/hardening slice, owning only two <=250-line held-out tests: seeded conservation/restart schedules and enumerated concurrent-admission races, with the original full scheduler gate. Direct @moe/core integration remains deferred because scheduler package.json/index/lock are outside ownership; children use the existing dependency-free scheduler convention and only structurally align with committed policy facts.

blockedReason: SPIDR split required: the original five-responsibility budget core cannot meet the enforced <=400 net-LOC and 1–3-file task size without oversized production/tests. Five bounded child tasks now own contract, ledger, protected reservation, measurement, and settlement slices. Planning this parent before those interfaces land would be speculative and could dispatch integration tests ahead of their producers.
